takeaways.label: Record revenue, NEET hit absorbed
takeaways.text: Q2 revenue of INR1,242 crores, up 18% YoY, was the highest ever, even as NEET demand softness persisted and the full-year gap remains unclosed.

takeaways.label: Online engine running at 34% core growth
takeaways.text: H1 core online grew 34%, driven by a 12.9% enrollment increase, Infinity Pro mix shift, and a 10x surge in Skills & Earners, while categories beyond JEE/NEET now contribute 74% of enrollments.

takeaways.label: Margins expanded 350 bps, H1 swung to profit
takeaways.text: Q2 EBITDA margin hit 18.8% on operating leverage and lower marketing spend, and H1 delivered a PAT of INR55 crores versus a INR57 crores loss last year.

takeaways.label: AI tutor and digital university are the next bets
takeaways.text: The Socratic AI tutor "Tuto" is live with 5,000+ learning hours and a paid launch imminent, while PW Digital University, India's first greenfield digital university, was gazetted in October.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether NEET crash courses close the delta, the pace of offline's march to breakeven, and any M&A closures from the online-first pipeline.

points.label: Core online momentum
points.text: H1 core online business grew 34%, exceeding internal targets, with Q2 online revenue up 26.4% YoY to INR694 crores. Unique enrollments rose 12.9% to 0.15 crore and ACPU increased 9.2% to INR4,280.

points.label: Infinity Pro driving mix shift
points.text: Infinity Pro collections quadrupled in Q2, with its share of collections rising to 35% from 31%, pulling up ARPU and student commitment.

points.label: Base broadening beyond JEE/NEET
points.text: Categories beyond JEE and NEET contributed 73.8% of H1 enrollments, up from 64.8% a year ago. Boards and CUET enrollments rose 130%, Foundation enrollments grew 15% with collections up 40%, and Vernacular enrollments jumped 77% to 1.2 lakh across 10 languages.

points.label: Skills & Earners scaling fast
points.text: Skills enrollment grew 10.3x to 1.69 lakh, and the PW Skills and Earners program grew 10x YoY, adding a new growth vector outside test prep.

points.label: Finance category leadership
points.text: The finance category (CA, CS, ACCA, CFA) grew close to 30%, making PW one of the leaders in professional finance courses across India.

points.label: South India organic push
points.text: Approximately 9% of H1 revenue came from South India, covering five states and 1.5 crore students, with an online-first playbook now amplified by AI live translation into 12 Indic languages. Management is confident to go organic and not target M&A for southern expansion.

quotes.text: Prateek Boob: "You can imagine this as the same set of teachers, which are the star teachers in respective exam categories. The students of all Indic languages will be getting benefited with this live AI translation of our batches."

sections.title: NEET: The Acknowledged Hit and the Recovery Bet

points.label: The NEET gap is real and quantified
points.text: Full-cycle online NEET collections are still 7% below last year and enrollments 13% lower, while offline NEET enrollments for the academic year are 8% lower. Management expects this gap to be reflected in full-year NEET numbers.

points.label: Demand timing helped Q2 but did not close the gap
points.text: NEET results were delayed to 16 July, pushing demand into Q2. Online NEET collections rose 27% and enrollments over 30% in the quarter, but the full-cycle deficit remains.

points.label: Offline took a double hit
points.text: The majority of the offline headwind came from NEET, where offline ARPU is significantly higher than online, creating a twofold impact in both PW and Xylem. Government exam notification delays further hurt Utkarsh Classes.

points.label: Xylem's concentration risk
points.text: Xylem saw impact because of 80% dependence on NEET with no other categories to recover; a strategy is now being put in place to reduce that dependence.

points.label: Crash courses as a partial fix
points.text: Aggressive NEET crash courses and mega crash courses are being launched earlier this year, both online and offline, in Q3 and Q4, with the aim of covering some of the NEET delta.

points.label: Medium-term recovery thesis
points.text: Management expects NEET demand to recover over the medium to long term, supported by the anticipated transition to a computer-based examination format in FY 2028 and structural expansion of India's medical education system.

quotes.text: Alakh Pandey: "Definitely there is a hit of NEET, and we are not shying away from it. Definitely there is a NEET hit in online as well as in offline."

points.label: Record admissions, Vidyapeeth the anchor
points.text: Offline scaled to 370 centers with the highest-ever H1 admissions of 4.13 lakh enrollments. Vidyapeeth contributed 66% of H1 offline revenue and did "phenomenally well."

points.label: Vidyapeeth turned profitable
points.text: The core offline Vidyapeeth business turned profitable at the stand-alone entity level, and overall offline is inching toward breakeven, with great improvement expected.

points.label: H1 loss narrowed
points.text: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA loss for offline reduced to approximately INR108 crores in H1 from approximately INR120 crores a year ago.

points.label: ARPU decline is a mix story, not a pricing one
points.text: Offline ARPU decline reflects mix change from newer centers. Vidyapeeth ARPU is 9–10% higher YoY in the core business, and the full ARPU story is expected to unlock at year-end when full revenue accrues.

points.label: Center expansion cadence
points.text: 25 to 30 new centers are planned annually for the next two to three years, with growth levers primarily in JEE and NEET, plus government examination offline centers targeting first- and second-year college students independent of notification cycles.

points.label: H2 recovery path
points.text: Q2 and Q3 are the strongest quarters for offline, with revenue recovery coming higher in Q3. H2 expansion costs are much lower than last year due to fewer new Vidyapeeth openings, and cost efficiencies and landlord negotiations are underway in subsidiaries.

points.label: AI Tuto (Socratic AI tutor) is live
points.text: The product is live at tuto.pw.live with more than 5,000 hours of learning completed and 4,000 students currently studying. It will be launched at larger scale at Vishwas Diwas.

points.label: Cost trajectory
points.text: AI Tuto's cost is already below INR20 per hour and will go down significantly in one or two quarters.

points.label: Pricing and monetization
points.text: Price discovery is yet to happen, but broad directional guidance points to pricing at double the ACPU of online batches. Very little monetization is expected this year as the product remains primarily experimental.

points.label: International aspirations
points.text: Management believes AI Tuto can fulfill international aspirations and is "quite bullish on these lines." The product will be available in 20 Indic languages and is designed to scale easily across categories.

points.label: AI live translation for batches
points.text: All important live batches will be available in 12 Indic languages for the next academic year, using live AI translation of star teachers, a capability already demonstrated and now driving South Indian distribution.

points.label: AI-driven headcount efficiency
points.text: The first sequential dip in total employees and faculty count was driven by AI efficiencies in content making, quality checks, test paper making, and test paper evaluation teams.

points.label: Tech investment rising
points.text: H1 tech spends reached INR104 crores versus INR70 crores last year, an increase of 1% as a percentage of revenue, with AI now writing 90% of code.

quotes.text: Prateek Boob: "This is the most superior product in terms of learning outcome and engagement which we have ever seen."

points.label: Q2 EBITDA margin expanded 350 bps
points.text: Q2 EBITDA margin reached 18.8% versus 15.3% last year, driven by leverage across most cost line items. Employee costs without ESOP were lower by 2.3% YoY, and marketing spends improved 1.2% as a percentage of revenue.

points.label: H1 swung to PAT profit
points.text: H1 delivered a PAT of INR55 crores versus a INR57 crores loss last year, on 21% revenue growth. Pre-Ind AS EBITDA reached INR190 crores, 2.6x last year's INR72 crores.

points.label: Full-year PAT positive commitment
points.text: Management is committed to closing the full year at PAT positive for H1 and H2 put together.

points.label: Online margin discipline
points.text: Management is confident to deliver online margins as guided, with no aggressive plans to shift margins into marketing. 100% EBITDA growth at the group level is expected to come mostly from online.

points.label: Intentional margin reinvestment
points.text: Online EBITDA margins could be increased, but management is instead investing in the AI tutor, with no plan to increase margins for the next two to three years.

points.label: Marketing leverage to continue
points.text: Marketing spends as a percentage of revenue improved 1.2% YoY, and management expects to continue seeing leverage as they improve ROCE and build efficiencies in newer categories.

points.label: PW Digital University incorporated
points.text: India's first greenfield digital university was officially notified in the Punjab Government Gazette effective October 29. It will offer undergraduate, postgraduate, and professional-level programs through online delivery, digital assessments, and virtual labs, with the admission cycle starting July next year.

points.label: Near-zero capital delivery model
points.text: The university will require near-zero capital allocation for course delivery, being 100% digital. It will merge test prep with university degrees, feature industry-led curriculum via PW Skills, and serve as forward integration for grade 12 students.

points.label: FinZ loan book sold
points.text: FinZ Finance signed a deed of assignment on October 3 with Auxilo Finserve Private Limited, selling the entire loan book for a consolidated consideration of INR96 crores. Student lending will now be offered through regulated third-party NBFCs, while FinZ continues as an RBI-registered NBFC until closure, subject to RBI approval.

points.label: Sarrthi IAS acquisition closed
points.text: PW acquired an 11% stake in Sarrthi IAS for INR71 crores, with the transaction consummated this quarter. PW is now the largest educator in civil services exam preparation in India in terms of enrollments and collections.

points.label: M&A pipeline active
points.text: A robust pipeline of education companies fitting the online and AI-first M&A strategy is in play, with advanced talks on a couple of online assets for category expansion. Deals are expected to be very margin accretive, with less than USD2 crore allocation from IPO proceeds, in line with the original plan of INR300 crores for unidentified M&A over three years.

points.label: IPO proceeds deployment
points.text: INR1,800 crores of IPO proceeds are to be utilized over the next two years, with capital allocated to South expansion and the AI tutor, though not in substantial amounts given the solid YouTube funnel playbook.

points.label: Investor Day scheduled
points.text: The first Investor Day is planned for November 18 in Mumbai, commemorating the first year of stock exchange listing, where AI Tuto will be showcased.

quotes.text: Amit Sachdeva: "We now have a very robust pipeline of education companies that fit into our M&A strategy of online and AI first. That has always been the color of companies that we have been looking at."

items.title: Offline centre profitability
items.text: The network grew from 198 to 370 centres by Q2 FY27, with record 4.13 lakh H1 offline enrolments and Vidyapeeth ARPU up 9-10% YoY. Management guides offline to turn full-year profitable in FY27 and targets steady-state margins of 13-15%, against -10% in FY26.

items.title: Socratic AI tutor launch
items.text: The AI tutor is live at tuto.pw.live with 5,000+ learning hours, and the first paid launch for grades 6-12 and JEE/NEET is synchronised to the academic cycle in 20 Indic languages. It is priced at roughly double online batch ARPU, creating a new AI-led revenue stream from FY28 as price discovery completes.

items.title: South India and Xylem scale-up
items.text: Xylem closes FY26 at ₹330-340 crore revenue versus ₹90 crore at acquisition, with 13 new centres opened and South India contributing 9% of H1 FY27 revenue. Vishwas Diwas FY27 sales showed South enrolment growth above 30%, with higher ARPU expected at steady state.

items.title: Premium online products and ARPU
items.text: Online ACPU rose 11.4% to ₹4,104 in FY26, and Infinity Pro collections grew 32% in Q2 FY27 with its share of collections up to 35%. ARPU gains come from premium tiers while base batch prices stay flat, lifting online margin without price increases on the core product.

items.title: State boards and vernacular
items.text: The state boards vertical, launched June 2025, reached 393k enrolments and was EBITDA positive in year one, with revenue up 9-10x FY25→FY26 against a 6-crore-student TAM. Q1 FY27 saw enrolments and revenue double as coverage expanded from 7 to 14 state boards.

items.title: PW Digital University
items.text: PWDU was notified in the Punjab Gazette effective October 29 as India's first greenfield digital university, with admissions opening in the July 2027 cycle. It merges test prep with degrees for the 70% of students who are 12th-plus, at near-zero capital allocation.

items.title: Earners skilling ramp
items.text: The Earners short-course platform, launched April 2026, crossed 1 lakh students and $1 million revenue in its first month, and Q2 FY27 skills enrolments grew 10.3x to 1.69 lakh. Management plans to double down on the 100% online format, adding a fast-growing category outside exam prep.

items.title: Sarrthi IAS subsidiary
items.text: Tranche II closed in Q2 FY27, lifting the stake from 40% to 51% and making Sarrthi a subsidiary; like-for-like nine-month revenue doubled and FY26 turnover reached ₹76.52 crore. This makes PW the largest civil-services educator in India by enrolments, in a category where UPSC enrolments doubled in FY26.

items.title: Asset-light K-12 build-out
items.text: Online K-12 revenue grew 88% YoY in Q1 FY27 to ₹105 crore, Curious Junior enrolments rose 67% with break-even expected this year, and SIP partnerships grew past 50 schools. Management expects K-12 to become a significant EBITDA contributor by FY29-30 in a market it sizes at 4x test prep.
